mainTopic: Whose תחום an animal or shared object follows on יום טוב, and the debate over ברירה (retroactive clarification).
overview: Our משנה says an animal given to a shepherd still follows the owner's תחום. A ברייתא of רבי דוסא says it follows the shepherd. The גמרא settles the clash: the ברייתא is a town with one shepherd, and the משנה is a town with two. The same split explains how רבי יוחנן can rule like רבי דוסא and also follow a סתם משנה. A ברייתא then teaches that a robe borrowed by two partners may only go where both of them may walk. רב and שמואל argue about a barrel and an animal bought together, which leads to the question of ברירה, whether a later division reveals what was true from the start. רב's students challenge his reason for the animal, and רב is silent. The גמרא reports a dispute between רבי הושעיא and רבי יוחנן about ברירה, reverses it, and then challenges רבי יוחנן's new position using a ruling about brothers who divide land and a ברייתא of איו about עירובין. That challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Our משנה seems to disagree with רבי דוסא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that our משנה does not match the view of רבי דוסא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is not in line with רבי דוסא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא claims that our משנה does not follow רבי דוסא. This line sets up the next step, where it quotes רבי דוסא's ברייתא to show the clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said an animal given to a son or a shepherd follows the owner's feet. The גמרא is about to show a ברייתא that rules the opposite for a shepherd. So it raises the possibility that the משנה and רבי דוסא disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: not in line with, not following the view of
a תנא whose ruling is quoted in the ברייתא

phrases.english: is not in accordance with Rabbi Dosa,

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי דּוֹסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה about an animal following its owner's feet.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה (an animal given to a shepherd follows the owner) seems to contradict רבי דוסא.

steps.title: The ברייתא of רבי דוסא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא. An animal that was bought, or given to a shepherd, before יום טוב follows the buyer or the shepherd, even if it was handed over only on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי דוסא says (some say אבא שאול says): If someone buys an animal from his friend on ערב יום טוב, even if the seller only handed it over on יום טוב, it follows the feet of the buyer. And if someone gives an animal to a shepherd, even if he only handed it over on יום טוב, it follows the feet of the shepherd.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source that proves the clash. רבי דוסא says an animal given to a shepherd follows the shepherd, but our משנה says it follows the owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To be 'like the feet' of someone means the animal may only walk where that person may walk on יום טוב. רבי דוסא holds that the animal already belongs to the buyer's or shepherd's area from before יום טוב, even though it was handed over later. That directly opposes the משנה's ruling for a shepherd.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is taught in a ברייתא
and some say (a different name for who said it)
like the feet of; it follows that person's תחום
he handed it over
shepherd

steps.confusionAlert: 'Like the feet of the shepherd' is not about who owns the animal. It is about how far it may walk on יום טוב, which depends on that person's תחום.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Dosa says,
and some say: Abba Shaul says,

phrases.aramaic: הַלּוֹקֵחַ בְּהֵמָה מֵחֲבֵרוֹ מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: one who buys an animal from his friend on the eve of the Festival,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא מְסָרָהּ לוֹ
phrases.english: even though he did not hand it over to him
until the Festival itself,
it is like the feet of the buyer.
And one who gives an animal to a shepherd,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא מְסָרָהּ לוֹ
phrases.english: even though he did not hand it over to him
until the Festival itself,
it is like the feet of the shepherd.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי דּוֹסָא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the claim in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה does not follow רבי דוסא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא: an animal given to a shepherd follows the shepherd's feet.

steps.title: One shepherd versus two shepherds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the משנה can still agree with רבי דוסא. The ברייתא is about a town with one shepherd, and the משנה is about a town with two shepherds.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say the משנה follows רבי דוסא, and there is no problem. Here (the ברייתא) is a case of one shepherd. There (the משנה) is a case of two shepherds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא removes the clash by saying the ברייתא and the משנה are talking about different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there is only one shepherd in town, it is clear from before יום טוב who will get the animal, so it already follows him. If there are two shepherds, nobody knows yet which one will get it, so it stays with the owner's feet. Both rulings can be true at the same time.

keyTerms.meaning: you can even say
and it is not a problem
here... there (two different cases)

phrases.english: You can even say it is Rabbi Dosa,
and it is not difficult:
here it is with one shepherd,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the ברייתא of רבי דוסא.

phrases.english: there it is with two shepherds.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי דּוֹסָא, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the clash between the משנה and the ברייתא from steps 1-2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (one shepherd vs. two shepherds)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and רבי דוסא disagree about any animal given to a shepherd.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי דוסא speaks of one shepherd, and the משנה speaks of two shepherds, so they do not disagree.

steps.title: The משנה's wording supports two shepherds
steps.stepSummary: The wording 'to his son or to the shepherd' shows the owner had not decided ahead of time, which fits the case of two shepherds.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also exact this way, since it teaches: 'to his son or to the shepherd.' Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer from the exact words of the משנה and accepts it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'to his son OR to the shepherd,' which shows the owner did not know beforehand who would take the animal. That uncertainty matches the case of two shepherds, where the choice is still open. So the answer from step 3 fits the משנה naturally.

keyTerms.meaning: the wording is also exact (supporting this)
since it teaches
learn from this (it is proven)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי דוסא's rule (the animal follows the shepherd) applies when there is only one shepherd. The משנה's rule (it follows the owner) applies when it is not yet clear who will take it.

phrases.english: It is also precise, since it teaches:
"to his son or to the shepherd,"
learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּיְקָא נָמֵי דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 3 from the משנה's wording.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה is about a case with two shepherds.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules like רבי דוסא
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that the הלכה follows רבי דוסא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The הלכה follows רבי דוסא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling that the הלכה follows רבי דוסא, so an animal given to a shepherd follows the shepherd.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This moves from explaining the sources to deciding the practical הלכה. It also sets up a problem, because רבי יוחנן has another general rule that seems to point the other way.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא who reports רבי יוחנן's teachings
the practical law follows...

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Dosa.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the practical ruling about רבי דוסא's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי דוסא: an animal given to a shepherd follows the shepherd's feet.

steps.title: Does this clash with following a סתם משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יוחנן could rule like רבי דוסא. He also holds that the הלכה follows a סתם משנה, and our סתם משנה says the animal follows the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? But רבי יוחנן said: The הלכה follows a סתם משנה. And we learned in the משנה: Animals and vessels are like the feet of the owner!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling by pointing to another rule of his own that seems to lead to the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סתם משנה is a ruling stated with no name attached, and רבי יוחנן holds the הלכה follows it. Our משנה states without a name that the animal follows the owner. So ruling like רבי דוסא seems to go against רבי יוחנן's own principle.

keyTerms.meaning: did he really say this?
but didn't he say
a משנה stated without naming who holds it
and we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yoḥanan say this?
But didn't Rabbi Yoḥanan say:
The halakha follows an unattributed mishna,
and we learned: Animals and vessels
are like the feet of the owner!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי דוסא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן follows a סתם משנה, and the סתם משנה says the animal follows the owner, which is the opposite of רבי דוסא.

steps.title: The one-shepherd answer solves this too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reminds us it already showed the משנה and רבי דוסא speak about different cases, so רבי יוחנן can follow both.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we already explain: here it is one shepherd, there it is two shepherds!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing back to its earlier answer from step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי דוסא speaks of one shepherd and the סתם משנה speaks of two, the two rulings never clash. רבי יוחנן can rule like רבי דוסא in the one-shepherd case and like the משנה in the two-shepherd case without contradicting himself.

keyTerms.meaning: didn't we already explain the case as...

steps.whatToRemember: In practice: with one shepherd, the animal follows the shepherd (רבי דוסא). With two shepherds, it follows the owner (the משנה). רבי יוחנן's rulings fit both.

phrases.english: But didn't we establish:
here it is with one shepherd,
there it is with two shepherds!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָאו אוֹקֵימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 by reusing the answer of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing back to the earlier split between the cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Ruling like רבי דוסא contradicts following the סתם משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: They cover different cases (one shepherd vs. two shepherds), so both rulings stand.

steps.title: A borrowed robe shared by two people with opposite boundaries
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a robe borrowed by two partners may only be taken where both partners are allowed to walk.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Two people borrowed one robe together. One wanted to wear it in the morning to the בית המדרש, and the other wanted to wear it in the evening to a wedding feast. One made an עירוב תחומין to the north, and the other made one to the south. The one who went north may walk north with the robe only as far as the one who went south is allowed to walk. And the one who went south may walk south with the robe only as far as the one who went north is allowed to walk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a new case: two people share one borrowed robe, but each has set up his walking area in a different direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that a shared object is tied to the 'feet' of both partners. So the robe can only go to places that are inside both people's walking areas. Even if one partner can walk far to the north, the robe cannot go past the point where the southern partner's area ends.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Rabbis taught": this opens a ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה
A robe or long garment
In partnership, owned or borrowed together
He made an עירוב תחומין, which moves his 'home base' so he can walk further in one direction on שבת or יום טוב
"Like the feet of": the object may only go where that person may go

steps.confusionAlert: Each person can still walk his own full distance without the robe. The limit applies only to the robe, because it belongs to both of them.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Two people who borrowed one robe together in partnership,

phrases.aramaic: זֶה לֵילֵךְ בּוֹ שַׁחֲרִית לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ,
phrases.english: this one to go in it in the morning to the study hall,

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶה לִיכָּנֵס בּוֹ עַרְבִית לְבֵית הַמִּשְׁתֶּה.
phrases.english: and that one to go in it in the evening to the wedding feast.
This one made an עירוב for himself to the north,
phrases.notes: An עירוב תחומין shifts where your שבת walking limit is measured from, letting you go further in that direction.

phrases.english: and that one made an עירוב for himself to the south.
The one who made an עירוב for himself to the north

phrases.aramaic: מְהַלֵּךְ לַצָּפוֹן כְּרַגְלֵי מִי שֶׁעֵרַב עָלָיו לַדָּרוֹם.
phrases.english: may walk north with it only as far as the one who made an עירוב to the south may go.
And the one who made an עירוב for himself to the south

phrases.aramaic: מְהַלֵּךְ לַדָּרוֹם כְּרַגְלֵי מִי שֶׁעֵרַב עָלָיו לַצָּפוֹן.
phrases.english: may walk south with it only as far as the one who made an עירוב to the north may go.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁשָּׁאֲלוּ חָלוּק אֶחָד בְּשׁוּתָּפוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The רבי דוסא discussion is finished, and this ברייתא opens a new topic: objects shared by two people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A jointly borrowed item may only be carried where both partners are allowed to walk.

steps.title: When the two boundaries only meet at the house
steps.stepSummary: If the two walking areas overlap only at the house, the robe may not be moved at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they made their boundaries meet in the middle, then neither of them may move the robe from its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds the extreme case: the two partners' walking areas overlap only at one point, the house where the robe is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same rule as before. Suppose one partner's area ends at the house on its north side and the other's ends at the house on its south side. Then there is no shared space beyond the house, so the robe cannot go anywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: They placed something in the middle; here, their boundaries meet at the middle point
The walking limit on שבת or יום טוב
He may not move it

steps.whatToRemember: A shared object follows the 'feet' of all its owners. It may only go to the area that all their walking limits have in common, and if they share no area, it stays in place.

phrases.english: And if they made the boundary meet in the middle,
phrases.notes: He means each one placed his עירוב so far away that his limit ends exactly at the house.

phrases.english: then this one may not move it from its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם מִצְּעוּ אֶת הַתְּחוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the robe rule from step 8 to the case where there is no shared area at all.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the partners' limits meet only at the robe's location, the robe may not be moved.

steps.title: רב: a shared barrel is permitted, a shared animal is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא records a case of two partners who bought a barrel and an animal together. רב permits the barrel and forbids the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: Two people bought a barrel and an animal together in partnership. רב said: The barrel is permitted, but the animal is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case argued by the אמוראים: partners who bought a barrel of wine and an animal together and divide them on יום טוב. This step gives רב's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the robe, the wine and the meat get divided, so each partner ends up with his own share. רב says each partner may take his share of wine as far as he himself may walk. But the animal's meat is still limited to the area both partners share. The text here does not yet explain why the two cases differ.

keyTerms.meaning: "It was said": this introduces a מחלוקת of the אמוראים
A barrel, here of wine
An animal, bought to be שחט and divided
Permitted / forbidden; here, whether each may take his share beyond the shared area

steps.confusionAlert: רב is not saying the barrel has no limit at all. Each partner's share of wine follows that partner's own walking limit, not both partners' limits.

phrases.english: It was said:
Two people who bought a barrel and an animal together in partnership,
phrases.notes: They bought them before יום טוב and are dividing the wine and meat on יום טוב.

phrases.english: רב said: The barrel is permitted,
but the animal is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁלָּקְחוּ חָבִית וּבְהֵמָה בְּשׁוּתָּפוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a borrowed item that stays whole to bought items that the partners divide.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: each partner may take his share of the barrel within his own limit, but the animal stays limited to both partners' shared area.

steps.title: שמואל: even the shared barrel is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב and says the barrel is also forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: The barrel is also forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the other side of the מחלוקת. He treats the barrel the same way רב treats the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that the animal is forbidden. They argue only about the barrel. For שמואל, even the wine is still limited to the area both partners share. The גמרא will go on to examine רב's reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, too

steps.whatToRemember: רב: barrel מותר, animal אסור. שמואל: both אסור. They agree about the animal and argue only about the barrel.

phrases.english: And שמואל said: The barrel is also forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: חָבִית נָמֵי אֲסוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רב's ruling in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל: both the barrel and the animal are limited to the area both partners share.

steps.title: How can רב split the barrel from the animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב holds about ברירה. Either answer seems to force the barrel and the animal to have the same law.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does רב think? If he holds יש ברירה, the animal should be permitted too. If he holds אין ברירה, the barrel should be forbidden too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's split ruling from Step 10, where he permitted the barrel but forbade the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether we may say, after the partners divide something, that each piece was always that partner's piece. If we may (יש ברירה), both items should be permitted. If we may not (אין ברירה), both should be forbidden. Either way, רב's middle position looks inconsistent.

keyTerms.meaning: Retroactive clarification: something decided later counts as if it was decided from the start
We do say a later choice clarifies what was true all along
We do not say a later choice clarifies the past
Should be permitted

steps.confusionAlert: ברירה here is not about choosing on יום טוב. It asks whether dividing the item later shows which half belonged to each partner from the very beginning of יום טוב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This question frames the rest of the sugya, which is about whether ברירה works.

phrases.english: What does Rav hold?
If he holds there is retroactive clarification,
phrases.notes: He means: once the partners split the item, we say each one's share was his from the start of יום טוב.

phrases.english: then even the animal should be permitted!
And if he holds there is no retroactive clarification,
then even the barrel should also be forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָסָבַר רַב? אִי קָא סָבַר יֵשׁ בְּרֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling from Step 10, which שמואל disputed in Step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's distinction between the barrel and the animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma: whichever view of ברירה רב holds, both items should have the same law

steps.title: A live animal is different
steps.stepSummary: רב holds יש ברירה, but an animal's parts draw from each other, so the shares stay mixed together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, רב holds יש ברירה. But an animal is different, because its parts feed off each other, so the two partners' areas get mixed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב does hold יש ברירה. The animal is forbidden for a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine in a barrel can be cleanly divided, so ברירה works there. A live animal is one body whose parts nourish each other. Each partner's portion therefore keeps taking in something from the other partner's portion, and the two shares stay mixed.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (it introduces the true answer)
It is different
They draw / suck nourishment
From each other

phrases.english: Really, he holds there is retroactive clarification,
but an animal is different,
since the limits draw from one another.
phrases.notes: The parts of a living animal feed each other, so each partner's share keeps mixing with the other partner's.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם קָסָבַר יֵשׁ בְּרֵירָה, וְשַׁנְיָא בְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma in Step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Picks one side of the dilemma and gives a special reason for the animal
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב must hold either יש ברירה or אין ברירה for both items
steps.terutzMaskana: רב holds יש ברירה. The animal is forbidden only because its parts feed each other, which mixes the shares.

steps.title: רב כהנא and רב אסי object, and רב is silent
steps.stepSummary: רב's students ask why the חכמים would ignore מוקצה but worry about תחומין. רב does not answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא and רב אסי said to רב: the חכמים did not worry about מוקצה, yet they did worry about תחומין? רב was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: Two of רב's students attack his answer from Step 13, and רב gives no response.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The students say it is inconsistent to ignore one concern, מוקצה, but to be strict about another, the mixing of תחומין. רב's silence shows that he had no answer to this challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Something set aside and not available for use on שבת or יום טוב
The walking limits for שבת and יום טוב
They were concerned
He was silent

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא וְרַב אַסִּי לְרַב
phrases.english: Rav Kahana and Rav Asi said to Rav:
About the prohibition of muktzeh they were not concerned,
yet about the prohibition of limits they were concerned?!
Rav was silent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא וְרַב אַסִּי לְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's reason that the animal's parts draw from each other
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is inconsistent to be lenient about מוקצה but strict about תחומין in the same case

steps.title: What is the final view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the conclusion is on this question.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was decided about this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next step by asking where the law ends up on ברירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge to רב's explanation was left unanswered (שתיק רב), so the גמרא moves to the broader view of other אמוראים about ברירה.

keyTerms.meaning: What was concluded about it?

phrases.english: What was concluded about it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הָוֵי עֲלַהּ?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on after רב's silence
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The final view on whether ברירה works

steps.title: רבי הושעיא says yes, רבי יוחנן says no
steps.stepSummary: רבי הושעיא holds יש ברירה, and רבי יוחנן holds אין ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי הושעיא said: there is ברירה. רבי יוחנן said: there is no ברירה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a disagreement between two אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither view makes רב's split. According to רבי הושעיא, both the barrel and the animal are permitted. According to רבי יוחנן, both are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא. This report says he holds יש ברירה, but step 19 reverses it.
An אמורא. This report says he holds אין ברירה, but step 19 reverses it.

steps.whatToRemember: As first reported, רבי הושעיא holds יש ברירה, so both items would be permitted, and רבי יוחנן holds אין ברירה, so both would be forbidden. The גמרא challenges this report in steps 17-18 and swaps the two names in step 19. רב's middle position was left without an answer.

phrases.english: Rabbi Hoshaya said: There is retroactive clarification.
And Rabbi Yochanan said: There is no retroactive clarification.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא אָמַר: יֵשׁ בְּרֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A dispute: רבי הושעיא holds יש ברירה, and רבי יוחנן holds אין ברירה

steps.title: Does רבי הושעיא really hold there is ברירה? The doorway משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבי הושעיא's view and quotes a משנה about a dead body in a house with many doorways.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי הושעיא really hold יש ברירה? We learned: if a dead body is in a house with many doorways, all of them are impure. If one door is opened, only that one is impure. If a person intended to take the body out through one doorway, or through a window four by four, that saves all the doorways.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge to רבי הושעיא by quoting a משנה. This step sets up the attack, and the actual point against him comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every doorway is impure because the body might leave through any of them. Once the exit is decided, by opening a door or by a person's intention, the other doorways become pure. The גמרא will use this case to ask how רבי הושעיא understands that decision.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn in a משנה?
Doorways
He intended / planned
Window
It saves / protects

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Hoshaya hold there is retroactive clarification?
But didn't we learn in a mishnah:
A dead body is in a house, and it has many doorways:
all of them are impure.
If one of them was opened,
it is impure, and all the others are pure.
If he intended to take it out through one of them,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ בַּחַלּוֹן שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה
phrases.english: or through a window that is four by four,
it saves all the doorways.
phrases.notes: His plan alone is enough to protect the other doorways from becoming impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא יֵשׁ בְּרֵירָה? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the view of רבי הושעיא stated in Step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי הושעיא's view that יש ברירה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sets up a משנה about choosing a doorway for the body. The point drawn from it against רבי הושעיא comes in the next part of the גמרא.

steps.title: רבי הושעיא only purifies the doorways from now on
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends with a dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל about when the decision must be made. רבי הושעיא explains that בית הלל's later decision purifies the doorways only from that moment on, not backwards. This shows he holds אין ברירה, which contradicts step 16.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say the other doorways are pure only if he decided which doorway to use before the person died. בית הלל say it works even if he decided after the death. רבי הושעיא said this means the doorways become pure from now on. From now on, yes; backwards in time, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the משנה it began quoting in step 17 and adds רבי הושעיא's comment on it. This completes the challenge against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי הושעיא held יש ברירה, a later decision would show that this doorway was 'the' doorway all along, so the other doorways would never have been impure. Since he says the decision works only from now on, he must hold אין ברירה. That contradicts step 16, where he was said to hold יש ברירה.

keyTerms.meaning: Doorways or openings of the house
He thought about it, meaning he decided
From now and onward
Backwards in time, going back to the start

steps.confusionAlert: בית הלל do allow a decision made after the death. The challenge is not about whether the decision works at all. It is about whether it works only from now on or also backwards in time.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:
And this is only when he thought about it
phrases.notes: He means he decided which doorway the body would be taken out through.

phrases.english: before the dead person died.
And Beit Hillel say:
even after the dead person died.
And it was said about it,
Rabbi Hoshaya said:
to make the doorways pure
from now and onward.
From now and onward: yes,
backwards in time: no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִתְּמַר עֲלַהּ, אָמַר רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא: לְטַהֵר אֶת הַפְּתָחִים מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quoted source and the challenge that step 17 began.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 16's claim that רבי הושעיא holds יש ברירה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי הושעיא lets the later decision purify only from now on and not backwards in time. That fits אין ברירה, not יש ברירה.

steps.title: Reverse the two opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא swaps the names: רבי הושעיא holds אין ברירה and רבי יוחנן holds יש ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse it: רבי הושעיא says there is no ברירה, and רבי יוחנן says there is ברירה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by switching which opinion belongs to which אמורא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of explaining away רבי הושעיא's comment on the משנה, the גמרא fixes the earlier report from step 16. Now רבי הושעיא is consistent, but רבי יוחנן becomes the one who holds יש ברירה. That sets up the next challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse it, swap the opinions
A later choice does not reveal what was true from the start
A later choice reveals what was true from the start

phrases.english: Reverse it,
phrases.notes: Swap the two names given in step 16.

phrases.english: Rabbi Hoshaya said: there is no retroactive designation,
and Rabbi Yochanan said: there is retroactive designation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵפוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reversing the attribution of the opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי הושעיא holds יש ברירה and רבי יוחנן holds אין ברירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי הושעיא holds אין ברירה and רבי יוחנן holds יש ברירה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says brothers who divide count as buyers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reversed version. רבי יוחנן ruled that brothers who split an inheritance count as buyers and must return their shares at יובל, which sounds like אין ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does רבי יוחנן really hold of ברירה? Didn't רב אסי say in the name of רבי יוחנן: brothers who divided their inheritance are counted as buyers, and they return the land to each other at יובל?
steps.whatsHappening: Right after the swap, the גמרא challenges the new claim that רבי יוחנן holds יש ברירה, using another ruling of his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With יש ברירה, each brother's share would be shown to have been his from the father's death, so he would be an heir and not a buyer. רבי יוחנן says they are buyers and must give the land back at יובל. That means he does not use ברירה here.

keyTerms.meaning: Brothers who divided an inheritance
Buyers, people who purchased
The fiftieth year, when bought land goes back to its original owners
The אמורא who reports רבי יוחנן's ruling

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּרֵירָה?
phrases.english: But does Rabbi Yochanan hold of retroactive designation?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Asi say that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Brothers who divided
are buyers,
phrases.notes: Each brother counts as having bought his share from the others, not as having inherited it directly.

phrases.english: and they return it to each other in the Jubilee year.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּרֵירָה? וְהָאָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the new version of the opinions set up in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim from step 19 that רבי יוחנן holds יש ברירה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ברירה applied, each brother would be an heir from the start. Calling them buyers who return their shares at יובל shows אין ברירה.

steps.title: Maybe רבי יוחנן rejects ברירה only in Torah law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יוחנן's אין ברירה applies only to Torah laws, while in rabbinic laws he holds יש ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: when does רבי יוחנן not hold of ברירה? In Torah laws. But in rabbinic laws, he does hold of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a way out of the contradiction from step 20. It splits רבי יוחנן's view into two areas: Torah law and rabbinic law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inheritance and יובל case in step 20 is a Torah law, so there רבי יוחנן says אין ברירה. In rabbinic laws he could still say יש ברירה, which would fit the swapped version from step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say. This opens a suggested answer.
A law from the Torah itself
A law set up by the חכמים
He does not hold of it

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא: כִּי לֵית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּרֵירָה —
phrases.english: And if you will say: when does רבי יוחנן not hold of ברירה?
In Torah law, but in rabbinic law he does hold of it.
phrases.notes: So the inheritance case from step 20 is Torah law, and that is the only place he would say אין ברירה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20 by limiting רבי יוחנן's אין ברירה to Torah law.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: a Torah law versus a rabbinic law distinction
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's inheritance ruling shows he holds אין ברירה everywhere, which contradicts the swapped version.
steps.terutzMaskana: He holds אין ברירה only in Torah laws, and יש ברירה in rabbinic laws.

steps.title: Does he really accept ברירה in rabbinic law? Look at איו's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רבי יוחנן accepts ברירה even in rabbinic law, and brings a ברייתא taught by איו.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in rabbinic law, does he hold of it? Didn't איו teach otherwise?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 21. It opens with a source, איו's teaching, that it is about to quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is aimed at the claim that רבי יוחנן holds יש ברירה in rabbinic law. This line only introduces the source, and the actual content comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Does he hold of it? Asked with doubt, expecting the answer no.
But wasn't it taught? This introduces a source used to challenge.
A תנא who taught this ברייתא

phrases.english: And in rabbinic law, does he hold of it?
But didn't איו teach:

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִדְרַבָּנַן מִי אִית לֵיהּ? וְהָתָנֵי אַיּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוחנן holds יש ברירה in rabbinic law
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rabbinic-law source, איו's ברייתא about עירוב, seems to reject ברירה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: you cannot set a condition between two sages
steps.stepSummary: איו's ברייתא: רבי יהודה allows a condition about which direction a sage comes from, but not a choice between two sages coming from two directions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: a person cannot make a condition about two things at once. Rather, if a sage comes from the east, his עירוב is in the east, and if from the west, his עירוב is in the west. But if sages come here and there, he cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the content of איו's ברייתא. It sets up the challenge against רבי יוחנן, and the link to him continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב תחומין is a rabbinic law. רבי יהודה forbids a person to put down two עירובין and choose later on שבת which sage to go hear. Deciding later which עירוב counted from the start is ברירה, so רבי יהודה seems to reject ברירה even in a rabbinic law.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes a condition
Here an עירוב תחומין, food placed down to set where a person's שבת home is, which lets him walk further in that direction
A sage, here one coming to teach on שבת
Here and there, meaning two sages in two directions

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. One sage whose direction is unknown is allowed. Two sages, where the person picks one later on שבת, is not allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the attack on step 21. If רבי יוחנן follows this ruling, then he rejects ברירה even in rabbinic law.

phrases.english: רבי יהודה says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם מַתְנֶה עַל שְׁנֵי דְּבָרִים כְּאֶחָד,
phrases.english: A person may not make a condition about two things at once.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: אִם בָּא חָכָם לַמִּזְרָח — עֵירוּבוֹ לַמִּזְרָח,
phrases.english: Rather: if a sage comes to the east, his עירוב is in the east.
If to the west, his עירוב is in the west.
But if sages come here and there, he may not.
phrases.notes: He means two sages come, one on each side, and the person wants to decide on שבת which one to go hear.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵין אָדָם מַתְנֶה עַל שְׁנֵי דְּבָרִים כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the content of the source that step 22 introduced.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוחנן holds יש ברירה in rabbinic law
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה forbids choosing later between two עירובין, which looks like rejecting ברירה in a rabbinic law. The גמרא ties this to רבי יוחנן on the next amud.
